title: Trace-span enrichment pipeline and synthetic-latency explainer
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a lightweight trace-span enrichment pipeline and an accompanying synthetic-latency explainer dashboard that makes it easy for on-call and SRE teams to distinguish timeouts, overload, model errors, and transport-level faults (HTTP/gRPC).

Background: We currently capture raw spans and a handful of error counters but lack a consistent signal that attributes latency to one of the primary failure modes across the inference path: upstream client retries, gateway queuing/overload, runtime/model stalls (kv-cache/attention), and transport-layer failures. This ticket combines two deliverables: (1) a scalable enrichment pipeline that attaches failure-mode annotations to spans/events and emits derived metrics and logs; and (2) a dashboard that slices latency and error budgets by failure class with guided remediation steps.
acceptance_criteria: Trace enrichment service annotates >95% of inference traces with a canonical failure_mode tag (values: ok, client_timeout, gateway_overload, runtime_model_error, transport_error) for requests above the 95th latency percentile.
Derived metrics exported to metrics back-end: inferred_failure_count{failure_mode}, inferred_failure_rate{route}, inferred_p95_latency_by_failure_mode available for queries.
Synthetic-latency explainer dashboard exists in Console with pre-built filters: time window, route, model, region, and shows top 3 contributing spans and the inferred failure mode breakdown.
On-call playbook linked from the dashboard with remediation steps for each failure_mode and one example runbook for gateway_overload.
End-to-end test that injects synthetic traces (client retry, delayed runtime response, forced gRPC UNAVAILABLE) and validates annotation correctness in CI.
tasks: Design canonical failure_mode taxonomy and mapping rules (timeout thresholds, HTTP/gRPC code mappings, kv-cache stall heuristics)
Implement span enrichment lambda that subscribes to trace-forwarding topic and runs deterministic rules; provide a feature flag for sampling rate
Emit derived metrics and logs to metrics/logs pipeline (Prometheus-compatible metrics exporter + JSON logs to ELK)
Create synthetic trace generator harness and CI validation job
Design and ship Console dashboard panels and an embedded runbook link
Performance test enrichment pipeline at 2x peak QPS and validate <2ms latency added per trace
comments: 2025-02-20 Aisha Patel: Created ticket and initial taxonomy proposal attached. Early stakeholders: SRE, Runtime, Console UX. Recommend iterative rollout behind feature flag.

2025-02-25 Marcus Liu: Prototype of enrichment lambda implemented. Early results: client_timeouts and transport_error correctly detected in 87% of sampled traces; runtime_model_error needs better heuristics (KV cache stalls not yet captured).
2025-02-28 Sofia Rodriguez (SRE): Reviewed mapping table; suggested adding a 'probable_model_stall' score instead of binary flags to help triage and reduce false positives from long generations.
2025-03-03 Marcus Liu: Added probabilistic scoring field (model_stall_score) to span schema and updated exporter. Pushed PR (link above). Working on metrics exporter and dashboard panels.
2025-03-05 Product review: PM Tom Nguyen asked to include per-customer breakdown for Dedicated tenants and confirm PII-free logs. Marcus updated logs to avoid request payloads.

2025-03-06 Marcus Liu: Load test results attached to PR; enrichment lambda adds 1.4ms median additional latency and <2% CPU on 4-core service. Moving to in-review for instrumentation and Console panels.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: deterministic rule-based enrichment vs ML classifier. Decision: start with deterministic rules to keep explainability and low runtime cost; plan ML model in Q3 if noise remains high.
KV-cache stall detection heuristic: look for long-running model forward spans with zero token emission events and repeated KV cache miss markers from runtime logs.
Privacy: enrichment only attaches high-level failure_mode tags and aggregated metrics; no prompt text is forwarded. Confirmed with Security (email thread in confluence link).
